column2: Propose The Israelites fled for They fled after the foreigners' attack. The Greek leaves the fleeing subject unexpressed, but the opposing sides and verse 7's explicit Israel had fled identify it contextually; the English pronoun could otherwise suggest that the foreigners fled. Retain foreigners, Mount Gelboue and fell wounded; the close draft preserves the pronoun.
Retain repeated foreigners, pursuit of Saul and sons and the three named sons struck. The selected Amminadab form is not changed to a parallel account's royal-son name.
Retain the heavy battle, archers, bows and pains and Saul suffering from the bows. The unusual coordination remains explicit rather than confidently supplying a specific arrow wound.
column3: How do pains and the following suffering verb relate to the archers' finding Saul in this selected construction?

column2: Retain Saul's request to his equipment carrier, sword, piercing, fear of mockery, refusal from fear and Saul's fall on the sword. The shorter selected request does not add another feared stabbing clause from a parallel account.
Retain the carrier seeing Saul dead, also falling on his own sword and dying. The sequence remains without an added motive beyond what the text states.
Retain Saul, three sons, that day and all his house dying together. All his house is not softened to avoid tension with descendants named elsewhere.
column3: What is the narrative scope of house here: the present royal company or a broader household? No exhaustive genealogical extinction is newly asserted.

column2: Retain every Israelite in the valley, the observed flight and deaths, abandonment of cities and the foreigners occupying them. The explicit Israel fled clause supports the contextual subject clarification in verse 1.

Retain the next day, plundering the wounded and finding Saul and sons fallen at Gelboue. Wounded is the selected casualty term; the context confirms these named bodies are dead without proving that the noun always means slain.

Retain stripping, taking head and equipment and announcing good news to idols and people throughout the foreigners' land. Good news represents the victors' announcement, not an endorsement by the translation.
Retain equipment in their god's house and the head in Dagon's house. No display method or different sanctuary detail is imported from Samuel.
Retain all Galaad's inhabitants hearing all that was done to Saul and Israel. Jabis is not inserted into this broader place designation before it appears in verse 12.

Retain mighty men from Galaad, Saul's body and singular the body of his sons, transport to Jabis, bones under the oak and seven days' fasting. The selected singular collective body and oak are not harmonized to another account.

Retain Saul's lawlessness against the Lord, failure to keep His word, consultation through the medium and the explicit Samuel the prophet answered him. Counsel is an inherited contextual object of seeking, not a separate Greek noun; the Samuel clause is not omitted or explained away.

Propose and the Lord killed him for and He killed him to distinguish Saul as the non-seeking subject from the divine killing and transfer of kingship. The Greek does not repeat the divine name as subject; the contextual inference is grounded in the immediately preceding Lord and the theological explanation. The close draft retains the inherited capitalization cue alone.
Retain all Israel at Hebron, behold and the bones-and-flesh kinship declaration. The plural bones remains rather than normalization to a singular bone formula.

Retain formerly for yesterday-and-third-day idiom, Saul's reign, David leading out and in and the Lord's shepherd/leader promise. Ordinary you addresses David inside both human and divine speech; My remains the Lord's first person.

Retain all elders, repeated Hebron, covenant before the Lord, anointing over Israel and the Lord's word through Samuel. The king already receives that title before the narrated anointing; the title is not deleted to reconstruct stages.
Retain the king and Israel's men, Jerusalem identified as Jebus and the resident Jebusites. The parenthetical identification remains distinct from the preceding Hebron setting.
Retain the prohibition of entry and capture of Zion's fortified enclosure, identified as David's city. No blind-and-lame taunt is supplied from a different account.
Retain the first attacker becoming ruler and general, Joab son of Sarouia ascending first and becoming ruler. Both the two promised titles and the shorter fulfilment title remain.
Retain David's residence in the enclosure and the resulting City-of-David naming. The explicit causal therefore links residence and name without an added conquest etymology.
Retain building around the city, fighting and taking it. The selected battle clause is not replaced by Joab restoring the remainder of the city from another witness.

Retain continued growth in greatness and the Lord Almighty's presence. Continued growing represents the repeated movement/growth construction; Almighty renders the selected title without inserting a Hebrew divine name.

Retain mighty-men rulers, strengthening with David and all Israel, the purpose of his reigning and conformity to the Lord's word about Israel. The collective support is not reduced to an individual hero's action.

Retain Jesebaal son of Achamani, first of thirty, drawing a sword once against three hundred wounded at one time. Sword, thirty and three hundred follow this selected account rather than a spear, three or eight hundred from a parallel.
column3: Does wounded here denote defeated casualties, and how should it be translated without asserting that all were already wounded before the action?

column2: Retain Eleazar son of Dodai the Achochi and membership among the three mighty men. The affiliation's attachment remains the inherited phrasing rather than a new family identification.
Retain Phasodomin, gathering foreigners, a barley-filled plot and the people's flight. Barley is not changed to the crop in a parallel heroic episode.
Retain singular he standing, saving the plot and striking the foreigners, followed by the Lord's great deliverance. The selected singular hero is not made plural with David by harmonization.
Retain three from thirty rulers, descent to the rock and Odollam cave, and the foreigners' camp in the Valley of the Giants. The explicit rock and giant designation remain.
Retain then for both David's enclosure and the foreigners' Bethlehem garrison. The paired temporal setting remains before the water request.

Retain David's desire and question about water from Bethlehem's gate cistern. The desired water is supplied as it contextually rather than treating the desire verb as having an explicitly stated object.
Retain the three breaking through, drawing gate-cistern water, bringing it to David, his refusal and libation to the Lord. Pouring is explicitly sacrificial here, not casual disposal.

Retain the divine-aversion idiom, blood of these men, repeated at-the-cost-of-their-lives interpretation, refusal and three-warriors summary. The inherited should not expresses the idiom's rejecting force, not an explicit negative particle in the first Greek clause.
column3: Does at the cost of their lives imply actual deaths too strongly, and would at the risk of their lives better convey the contextual idiom?

column2: Retain Abessa as Joab's brother and ruler of three, sword against three hundred wounded at one time and renown among three. The same casualty-term uncertainty as verse 11 remains; no parallel spear is imported.
Retain distinction among three above two, leadership and not attaining to three. The apparently competing rank statements are not silently resolved into a thirty/three hierarchy.
column3: Are distinct groups of three intended, or does the selected ranking require another syntactic or textual explanation?

column2: Retain Banaias son of Jodae, son of a mighty man, deeds beyond Kabasael, two ariels of Moab and a lion in a pit on a snowy day. Ariel remains unresolved rather than being confidently identified as men, lions or an altar type.
column3: How does beyond Kabasael relate to the deeds, and what entities does the plural ariel designate here?

column2: Retain the conspicuous five-cubit Egyptian, weavers' beam spear, Banaias's staff, taking the spear and killing with that spear. The exact height and weapon exchange remain without a modern unit conversion.
Retain Banaias's named summary and having a name among the three mighty men. The reputation formula is not changed to membership beyond what the clause warrants.
Retain honor above thirty, not attaining to three and appointment over David's ancestral house. House is not silently replaced by bodyguard or an added military office.
column3: Does the ancestral-house expression have an administrative household sense here?

column2: Retain the mighty-forces heading, Asael as Joab's brother and Eleanan son of Dodo from Baithlaem. The selected place form is preserved within the roster.
Retain Sammoth the Adite and Chelles the Phelonite as separate warriors. No parallel-roster names are substituted.
Retain Orai son of Ekkes the Thekoite and Abiezer the Anathothite. The patronymic and local affiliations remain.
Retain Sobochai the Asothite and Eli the Achoite. Similar names elsewhere do not warrant merging or normalizing these entries.
Retain both Netophathites, Moorai and Cholod son of Nooza. The shared locality does not erase the second patronymic.
Retain Aithi son of Ribai from Benjamin's hill and Banaias the Pharathonite. Hill is the selected common noun, not automatically a named town supplied from a parallel.
Retain Ouri from Nachaligaas and Abiel the Garabeththite. The opaque place form is not translated into an inferred valley system.
Retain Azmoth the Beermite and Eliaba the Salabonite. Both affiliations remain attached to their own names.
Retain Bennaias, Osom the Gennounite and Jonathan son of Sola the Ararite. The initial separate name is not merged into a sons-of phrase from another witness.
Retain Achim son of Sachar the Ararite and Elphal son of Our. The family and locality links remain separate.
Retain Ophar the Mochorathite and Achia the Phelonite. No alternate ethnic or geographical identity is supplied.
Retain Eserai the Charmalite and Naarai son of Azobai. The selected roster names are not conformed to Samuel's list.
Retain Joel as Nathan's brother and Mebaar son of Agari. Brother and son are distinct source relationships and are not flattened into patronymics.
Retain Selek the Ammonite and Nachor the Berthite carrying Joab son of Sarouia's equipment. The singular carrying participle identifies the second man contextually, not both as a plural pair.
Retain Ira and Gareb, both Jetherites. The repeated affiliation remains rather than a combined group replacing their names.
Retain Uriah the Chettite and Zabet son of Achlia. Uriah is not silently placed at the list's end to match a shorter parallel roster.
Retain Adina son of Saiza of Reuben, ruler and thirty alongside him. The selected thirty is not made an explicit total for the whole roster.
Retain Anan son of Moocha and Josaphat the Baithanite. The kingly-sounding second name does not establish a royal identification.
Retain Ozia the Astarothite and Samma and Jiiel as sons of Chothan the Ararite. The shared father belongs to the paired sons rather than Ozia.
Retain Jediel son of Sameri and Joazae his brother the Jeasite. The brother relation and affiliation remain in their selected order.
Retain Eliel the Miite, Jaribi and Josia his son, Elnaam and Jethema the Moabite. The selected son relation and separate Elnaam entry are not reorganized into a different paternal grouping.
column3: Does his son identify Jaribi as Josia's father, and how firmly do the selected name boundaries support that division?

column2: Retain Aliel, Obed and Jesiel the Misabite to close the roster. The singular affiliation remains with Jesiel rather than being silently made plural for all three.
